rationale: The 07:00 digest is a scheduled job on the same per-adult mail agent, with the same read-only Gmail tool and Google sign-in, and it waits on the same open decision (personal mail read by the cloud model with storage off); the roadmap lists the per-inbox mail agent and the 7:00 automation as deliverables of one milestone, M4 'Morning email digest', just as the school reader and its 16:00 digest are already one card (F051). Both are wave C, medium risk and read-only on one agent, so no riskier half is hidden and no agent boundary is crossed; round 1 kept the digest apart while it still carried a Gmail drafts write tool, which that same round took out, and the school mailbox (F051) and the owner-only mailout (F049, a send grant on another account and another agent) stay separate cards.
name: Per-person mail agent with read-only Gmail: 'did I get an email about X?' and a 07:00 digest of mail that needs action

rationale: The Places lookup is one tool on the research agent whose main use, by its own round 2 description, is place data (hours, ratings, a Maps link) for the outing planner, which lists it as a dependency, and the roadmap's M3 names the Maps connection as part of the same research and trip-planning build. Both are wave C on the memory-less research agent, the lookup is read-only and low risk so the card keeps the planner's medium risk, and the Google key with billing and the goplaces-or-Grounding-Lite choice become a decision stated on the one card, since the lookup record itself says a phone's maps app is quicker for a one-off question.
name: Trip and outing planner with Google Places lookup (day trip, weekend, multi-day; hours, ratings and a Maps link)

rationale: Both rest on one in-house journal of Happy's own writes in the household store: the weekly review reports from it and undo runs the inverse recorded in it, and the rows have to be written from inside each write tool (the store, the Reminders bridge, the calendar write, the reminder hook) because only there is the before-state known, so those tools are changed once for both, as round 2 noted on the undo record. Undo's wave C rests on no later dependency (everything it reverses is wave A or B) and both are medium risk on the parent's own agent; the card has to state the two parts separately, a read-only review first and undo as a second step that adds a guarded delete limited to items the journal shows Happy created, with forgetting a conversation still an operator command at the Mac.
name: What Happy did and what it remembered: a weekly review, undo of its last write, and forgetting a conversation on request

rationale: The only thing built for the practice quiz is one operator-reviewed skill, deployed through the same skills step in happy-deploy and loaded with the same `read` grant that the routines card adds to the parent's own agent, so the quiz is the first worked skill that proves that pipeline, as round 2 noted on the quiz record. Both are wave B on the same agent with no new tool; the card carries the quiz's medium risk and says that the photo route depends on photo reading (F002) and sends a worksheet to the cloud vision model unscreened, while a version the kids use themselves stays with the kids agent (F072).
name: Teach Happy a routine (operator-reviewed skills), with a parent-run practice quiz as the first one

rationale: Both are operator-only checks kept in the config repo and run after each change or update, with results that go to Tony alone: the health and audit scripts check the install, and the handful of behaviour cases check the agent through the eval harness that already exists, which round 2 said could ride on this card. Neither gives any agent a tool or touches live family data (the cases run against eval clones with fixtures) and both are low risk; the behaviour cases' wave B rests only on tools that three later cases need, so the four that apply today ship with wave A and the rest are added as those tools land.
name: Operator self-checks: daily integration health and credential expiry, security audit after every update and monthly, and behaviour cases in the eval suite

rationale: Talk is a control inside the same App Store app on the same phone, reached through the same single pairing, the same wave-A deny list (MAC-04) and the same tailnet route, and what the Talk card adds beyond that is one `talk` config block and four push-to-talk lines taken off the deny list. Both are wave D, high risk and limited to Tony's phone; round 2 left the pair apart, but its edits leave the two cards giving different instructions for that one pairing (the app card leaves Full or Limited access open because Full is what lets the app review approvals in general, the Talk card says to pair limited), which only one card can settle, and the merged card states Talk as an optional, experimental step with its own audio paths (Apple speech recognition on the phone, and raw audio to OpenAI on a separate key for the later realtime option).
name: OpenClaw iPhone app on Tony's phone: pairing with device commands denied first, chat with files, tap approvals, and optional Talk mode
